title: Vermont Farms - smart irrigation pilot scratch
content:
Quick capture from 11/03 call with Vermont Farms (Elaine M, Samir I). Informal notes / rough action list — keep for handoff to Eng + SEs.

Context
- Objective: small field pilot to use an LLM-based assistant for irrigation recommendations and anomaly detection using sensor streams (soil moisture, temp, rainfall, flow meters).
- Primary constraint: intermittent LTE connectivity at sites (cell drops 1-3x per day), local gateway required for offline inference and buffering.
- Timeline: POC cadence = 6 weeks (2 field sites), goal to demonstrate automated irrigation schedule + anomaly alerts.

People / Roles
- Elaine Morris (CTO, VF) — product owner for farm ops integration
- Samir Iqbal (Field engineer) — manages edge gateways/hardware
- Riya Patel (Redwood SE) — technical lead for model & deployment options
- Alex (VF ops) — daily user, will evaluate UX and alert quality

Hard requirements called out on the call
- Data residency: raw sensor telemetry must stay on-prem/edge; only derived alerts and anonymized summaries can be streamed to cloud.
- Security: gateway must support mutual TLS and customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).
- Offline mode: inference must continue with degraded model locally when connectivity is down.
- Latency: inline autoschedules need ~<300ms tail latency for decision loop (local). Cloud calls ok to be slower for non-real-time analytics.
- Throughput: average 120 inference calls / minute across both sites during peak (burst to 400/min possible during irrigation windows).
- Power/ram: gateways are mid-spec (8–16GB RAM, 4-core CPU, optional T4-class GPU later). Model footprint < 4GB preferred for local runs.

Model / inference considerations
- Preference for smaller causal models (7B-ish) quantized to int8 or int4 for on-edge. Need guidance from Redwood on expected quality vs quantization.
- Suggest two-tier model plan: local 7B quantized for immediate routing, cloud 13B+ for richer context/longer-term reasoning when connectivity available.
- KV cache not super useful for per-minute sensor queries; better to implement short-term state in gateway process instead of relying on large KV cache in cloud.

Operational gotchas (from VF and our experience)
- Clock drift across gateways -> time-aligned windows for sensor aggregation fail. Must enforce NTP and include fallback windowing logic.
- Intermittent duplicates from sensor bursts (debounce required). If we batch naively, duplicate batches cause noisy training signals.
- S3 endpoints blocked by VF network policies; need SFTP or S3 over private peering. Ask infra for supported protocols.
- TLS cert rotation cadence — VF ops rotates device certs monthly; ensure agent can re-provision without manual steps.

Prototype architecture (sketch)
1) Edge gateway (on prem) runs small Redwood runtime (container) with quantized 7B model. Handles: immediate inference, local state, buffering, mutual TLS to control plane when up.
2) Control plane (redwood hosted or Private) receives anonymized alerts + summaries; stores telemetry snapshots.
3) Cloud model (larger) available for batched reprocessing and offline analysis when gateway uploads.
4) Fallback policy: if gateway CPU/GPU overloaded, route to cloud when connectivity healthy; otherwise degrade gracefully to rule-based scheduler in agent.

Open questions to resolve
- Do VF gateways have GPUs? Samir to confirm exact SKU (edge boxes vs mini-servers).
- Can VF accept an agent container pull from our registry (air gap concerns)? If air-gapped, we need an image export workflow.
- What telemetry retention window on VF side for debug traces? They prefer 7 days on-site logs, then push selected artifacts to cloud.

Immediate next steps (owners)
- Samir: confirm gateway hardware + OS + cert rotation process (due 2025-11-07).
- Riya: run quick offline bench: 7B int8 on 8GB/16GB ram profiles, capture latency/throughput numbers and memory footprint (due 2025-11-10).
- Elaine: check legal on anonymization threshold for alerts; can we send sample anonymized payloads? (due 2025-11-09).
- SE/Eng: draft minimal Docker runtime image with metrics export endpoint and token-based bootstrap (Riya + Ben) (prototype due 2025-11-17).
- Create Jira VF-1234 subtasks for infra/network and security review (Riya).

Notes to self (Riya)
- Bring up the quantization trade-off doc in next sync — include example diff in watering suggestions between 7B int8 and 13B fp16.
- Add a small demo sequence that intentionally simulates disconnects (1hr window with toggled connectivity) to show graceful fallback.
- Consider recommending Dedicated reserved pool if they want consistent cloud fallback throughput (predictable latency during peak).

Risks and mitigation
- Risk: local model quality too low -> farmers distrust auto-schedules. Mitigation: conservative thresholds (alerts only), manual override button in UI, human-in-loop for first 2 weeks.
- Risk: certificate rotation breaks agent. Mitigation: automate cert rotation workflow and test in staging with monthly rotations.

Meeting artifacts to attach later
- demo recording link (Elaine requested)
- hardware spec PDF (Samir will upload)
- sample telemetry CSV for benchmark

End of scratch — will clean and formalize into a short pilot brief once we have the bench numbers and SAM's hardware confirmation.
